comment: Ep100 Switzerland vs Colombia (Play-Offs) — MILESTONE 100TH EPISODE — theme 'THE MARKSMAN AND THE GOLDEN CITY'. Switzerland = the legend of Wilhelm Tell (William Tell), the master crossbowman forced to shoot an apple off his own son's head, who never once missed his mark — a real, centuries-documented Swiss founding folk legend, symbol of Swiss precision and resistance, distinct from Legend 029's Alpine Guide, Legend 052's Watchmaker and Legend 089's Mountain motifs already used for Switzerland. Colombia = El Dorado, the Golden King, already carded as Legend 092 (and Legend 050/071/BONUS-1) — referenced here as flavor text only, NOT re-carded. OUR PREDICTION Switzerland 2-1 Colombia (Colombia strike first through Luis Díaz's pace; Embolo levels it 1-1; late, Xhaka — the captain who never misses — strikes the winner, a nod to Tell's arrow). Legend 100 = Wilhelm Tell, the Marksman (Switzerland). lines.text: Centuries ago, a marksman in the Swiss Alps was forced to shoot an apple off his own son's head. He never once considered missing. That is the legend of Wilhelm Tell.
And across the ocean, a different legend glitters — Colombia, chasing the golden city of El Dorado, a team that plays like it is already rich with talent.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — our milestone episode, one hundred. Switzerland, versus Colombia. A play-off. One shot, no second arrow.
Switzerland arrive with the coldest precision in the tournament. Colombia arrive with the flair and the golden swagger to match any side left standing.
Switzerland — the Marksman's nation. Built around a captain who never misses, and a defense as steady as an alpine wall.
Granit Xhaka, the captain — the general who reads every pass before it happens, and never, ever flinches on the big occasion.
Breel Embolo is the battering ram, the power that drags defenders backward every time he touches the ball.
Manuel Akanji is the king of calm, untroubled, unbothered, the defender who makes chaos look simple.
Ruben Vargas is the flyer out wide, all pace and directness, always hunting the byline.
And Yann Sommer is the wall in goal, veteran hands, the last line that so rarely gets beaten.
Colombia — chasing El Dorado. Technical, joyful, and carrying maybe the most dangerous front four left in this tournament.
James Rodríguez, the captain — the artist, still finding passes nobody else on the pitch can even see.
Luis Díaz is the lightning — bursting in behind at a speed defenders simply cannot plan for.
Jhon Durán is the cannon up front, all power, all violence in front of goal.
Richard Ríos is the engine in midfield, box to box, covering every blade of grass.
And Dávinson Sánchez is the tower at the back, dominant in the air, calm on the ball.
So here is the riddle. Does the Marksman's aim hold true? Or does the Golden City shine brighter tonight?
And stay with me — because on our milestone episode, this one turns on a captain's arrow, late.
Here is how we see it. Colombia come out flying, all rhythm and movement, looking for the first crack.
Díaz gets in behind on the left, the whole Swiss line dragged out of shape in a single stride.
And it lands! Colombia strike first — the golden city glitters, and their bench erupts.
Switzerland need an answer, and there is only one battering ram they trust to find it. Embolo goes hunting for the equaliser.
And Embolo finds it! One-one. Power, precision, exactly when Switzerland need him most.
But late, the captain drifts into space, and the whole stadium holds its breath, waiting for the arrow.
Xhaka strikes! Two-one, Switzerland. The captain never misses — not tonight, not on episode one hundred.
Two-one Switzerland. Colombia glittered brightly, but the Marksman found his mark exactly when it mattered.
Our prediction — Switzerland two, Colombia one. Xhaka, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And Colombia leave with their heads high — chasing El Dorado, who made the coldest defense in the tournament sweat for every single inch.
Switzerland march on. The Marksman's nation, precise as ever, still aiming for the trophy they believe is theirs to win.
So you tell me — the Marksman, or the Golden City? Comment SWITZERLAND for the Marksman — comment COLOMBIA for El Dorado.
They say his arrow never missed, not once, not even with his own son standing beneath it — the coldest nerve the Alps ever produced.
The players write the night. But Wilhelm Tell carries one truth — the mark is only found by the ones who never doubt the shot.
Here is how. Go to worldcup twenty-six dot world and create your free account — ten seconds, and Wilhelm Tell, Legend one-zero-zero, is yours.
Then pick three of the forty-eight nations, and every goal they score, scores for you. Free to play, just for glory.
So sign up tonight, claim your Legend, and send this to a friend who loves the beautiful game. Hit like, hit subscribe, and I'll see you at the next one.
